contentHtml:
Sept 21 (Reuters) - The Pennsylvania Department of Health reported 792 measles cases on Monday, 25 more than ​on Friday, as the state's outbreak grew ‌further, remaining at the center of the nation's worst measles resurgence in decades.

Here are some more details:

Sign up here.

  • The ​state health department confirmed 155 hospitalized measles ​patients, up from the 150 reported on ⁠September 18.

  • Lancaster County has remained the hardest-hit ​area in the state throughout the outbreak.

  • Earlier this ​month, Pennsylvania reported measles-related deaths among unvaccinated residents, a toll that sparked disagreement between Governor Josh Shapiro and U.S. Health ​Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. over how ​many fatalities were directly caused by the virus.

  • The Centers ‌for ⁠Disease Control and Prevention has not yet added Pennsylvania's 2026 measles deaths to its national count. The agency has said it is reviewing how ​it classifies ​such deaths.

  • The ⁠US has recorded 3,471 measles cases this year as of September ​17, according to CDC data.

  • Measles, a highly ​contagious ⁠viral disease, can cause fever, rash and respiratory complications, but is easily preventable with the measles, ⁠mumps ​and rubella vaccine, a routine ​childhood immunization that is 97% effective after two doses.

Reporting by ​Kamal Choudhury in Bengaluru; Editing by Shilpi Majumdar
